source.title: AP English Language and Composition – AP Students (College Board)
source.note: College Board numbers this course's units 1–9 without titles; StudySprint uses the same names (“Unit 1” and so on) and adds its own short description to each review guide's title. Each unit's “skills you will practice may include” list was read from this page on 2026-11-08 and is recorded as the unit's official topics.

frameworkCheck.title: AP English Language and Composition Course and Exam Description (effective Fall 2024)
frameworkCheck.how: The CED organizes this course by skills rather than content topics. Each unit's skill codes (for example 1.A, 3.A, 4.A in Unit 1) were read from the CED's Course at a Glance and cross-checked against the skills table, which lists the units for each skill; every skill code in a unit is matched to the StudySprint topic whose guide section and questions practice it.
frameworkCheck.unitWeightNote: College Board gives no exam weighting by unit for this course. The multiple-choice section weights eight skill categories: Rhetorical Situation – Reading 11–14%, Rhetorical Situation – Writing 11–14%, Claims and Evidence – Reading 13–16%, Claims and Evidence – Writing 11–14%, Reasoning and Organization – Reading 13–16%, Reasoning and Organization – Writing 11–14%, Style – Reading 11–14%, Style – Writing 11–14% (CED exam section, checked 2026-11-08).
frameworkCheck.examFormat: From the AP Students assessment page: 3 hours 15 minutes. Section 1, 45 multiple-choice questions (45% of the score) on excerpts from nonfiction texts: 23–25 reading questions and 20–22 writing questions that ask you to read like a writer and consider revisions. Section 2, 3 free-response questions (55%) in 2 hours 15 minutes including a 15-minute reading period: synthesis (an argument citing at least 3 of 6 sources), rhetorical analysis, and argument. StudySprint practice is multiple-choice only, in the same reading-passage and revision-draft style; free-response practice uses College Board's released questions.
differences: The AP Students page's skill lists are summaries in different words from the CED's numbered skills; both are recorded and both are build-checked.
